aj: Heads-up — after rolling the FP8 selector live in canary for H100/L40S (rfd-2027-03-10) we're seeing recurring ~12-20% tail latency spikes and a handful of batch rejection events. Repro window around 11:14 PDT. Attaching quick profiler dump and kv stats.

aj: ```
profile:
  kernel_select_ms: 1.9
  qkernel_fp8_dispatch_ms: 0.8
  fallback_int8_slowpath_ms: 8.2
kv_cache:
  hit_rate: 0.74
  eviction_seconds: 3.2
batches:
  median_size: 4
  rejected_count: 23
```

maria: Can you paste the kernel selector config used for the canary? curious whether TE (transformer engine) is in `automatic` mode or pinned. Also what batcher policy (latency-first / throughput-first)?

aj: Policy is `latency-first`, kernel_selector: `auto-quant-v3` (default TE settings). TE fp8 mode not explicitly set.

jonathan: This smells like a quant-switch flap: some layers pick the fp8 kernel while others fall back to int8/fallback kernels leading to layout transitions and extra memcpy/growth in KV churn. That can blow up per-token cost and evict the KV cache more often.

sarah: Agree. KV hit_rate 0.74 is pretty low for steady-state chat. If eviction_seconds ~3s that's aggressive for L40S with current KV config. Might be falling back to cold cache frequently causing the slowpath.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout rfd-2027-03-10 started on pool h100-pool-3 at 2027-03-10T11:10:12Z :rocket:

aj: Ran internal metric query: `curl -s -X POST /internal/metrics/query -d "metric=kv_evictions&since=30m"` -> shows eviction rate spike aligned with the tail-latency spikes.

jonathan: Quick mitigation: pin the kernel selector to `fp8_nn_int8_fallback:v2` (deterministic ordering) or disable automatic quant switching in TE for the canary and see if the spikes go away. Also try a slightly higher `kv_idle_timeout` (e.g. 8s -> 20s) to reduce churn.

maria: I'll add an e2e perf test that keeps a longer conversation open to stress KV lifetime; also can repro locally with smaller batcher to mimic the canary traffic shape.

sarah: Also check transformer-engine config: if `use_sparse_mlp` or `prefetch_kv` flags differ between kernels, that can cause memory pressure changes. And check kernel occupancy counters — sometimes the fp8 kernel reduces occupancy and shifts scheduling, oddly raising context switch overhead.

aj: pprof capture: https://pprof.internal/runs/2079003456 — contains CPU + GPU kernel dispatch timeline.

jonathan: If we can't find a quick safe fix, rollback the canary (rfd-2027-03-10) and re-run with pinned config. The rollback is cheap compared to SLA hits.

maria: I'll make the canary change to pin the selector and extend kv timeout in a new canary (rfd-2027-03-11) and monitor.

aj: Thanks — prepping rollback plan now, will post results in this thread in a few mins.

infra-bot: action: rollbacks_ready set by aj at 2027-03-10T11:20:55Z

aj: Quick note: observed one oddity — when the batcher rejects a request it sometimes forces the request to route to the fallback model family which uses different KV key format. That mismatch may be a separate bug (kv key schema drift) — filing follow-up issue.

sarah: Good catch. If key format drifts we'll see almost 0% hit-rate for those sessions. Please include a small debug trace for a rejected request.

aj: Will attach trace + logs when I push the rollback.

maria: cc @sre — can we raise the alert threshold for the canary pool so we don't noisy-page on transient 5m blips?

jonathan: +1 but keep a short SLA guardrail so we catch real regressions.

aj: Rolling back now, will update thread. :thumbsup:
